details: The US Federal Reserve maintained interest rates on October 28, but a split vote with two members favoring a hike underscored persistent inflation concerns. Data released by the Bureau of Economic Analysis on October 29/30 showed the core Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Fed's preferred inflation gauge, remained elevated at 3.1% year-on-year for September. This figure, above the Fed's 2% target, is leading markets to increasingly price in the likelihood of another rate hike in December.
title: US Core PCE Inflation Holds at 3.1%, Fuels December Fed Hike Bets

details: On October 30, Bitcoin Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs) experienced significant capital flight, recording a massive $643.2 million outflow. This marks the largest single-day withdrawal since June, reflecting a notable decline in investor confidence. Concurrently, Ethereum ETFs have endured eleven consecutive days of outflows, collectively erasing the gains they had accumulated throughout October.
title: Crypto ETFs See Major Outflows, Bitcoin Loses $643M in a Day

details: The International Monetary Fund (IMF), in its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, projects global inflation to remain elevated at 4.1% in 2027. This forecast includes numerous economies revising their inflation expectations upward. Such persistent high inflation, coupled with a global tightening of financial conditions, is increasingly challenging the established narrative of Bitcoin serving as a reliable inflation hedge for investors.
title: IMF Global Inflation Outlook Challenges Bitcoin as Inflation Hedge
